items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1966-01-20
items.q: So whenever he hired me, I'd either play down there with Punch or play with Bill and Diddy.

ctx.x: Who do you play at in Preservation? Who do you play with down there?

With Bill and Diddy. Mm-hmm. And Kid Punch. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Mac Jeffrey was hiding there all the time with Bill and Diddy while Nelson and them was away, you know? So whenever he hired me, I'd either play down there with Punch or play with Bill and Diddy. Mm-hmm. But at the hospital, that was my project. And I hired who I want to hire. Mm-hmm. So I had a keg ladder myself and uh, After you Proyber, Andrew Martin and Lars Trottet on drums.
How many pizzas is that? Six or five? Six. Yeah. Banjo?

items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1961-08-15
items.q: I think that was when Punchy first decided to go off. Went off of the show or something like that.

ctx.x: I've seen the name and the picture of their band.

Yeah, well I played with them and then Sam and Cornish got in a little misunderstanding and he split up. And Cornish made up his own band, well I went with Cornish. And I left off a clarinet then and went on sax, and John went in the band on clarinet. Cornish was on trombone and we had Wood and Joe playing Cornish. That was the lineup, you know, in that band. And I played with him a while. And finally Jack Kerris band made a split. And at that time his name was Fame around here, you know. Yeah, her mother, Punchy…
